feedback: This is the final iteration, so no later revision can use the race result. The candidate is identical to iteration 7, the best raced design (125.3), which is the only design with oval progress above 0.5 at base_speed 1.3 (iteration 7 oval progress 0.61). Iterations 8, 9 and 10 each changed one or two variables from this base (kp 3.5 with wheel_track 0.11 at 108.4; 16 mm footprint at 84.4; base_speed 1.15 at 108.5) and all scored lower, so the base has not been beaten by any tested single change. The candidate is valid: five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.02 to +0.02 and y = 0.03 are within range, the weights are antisymmetric in [-2, 2], and kp, ki, kd, base_speed, mass, wheel_track and line_loss are in range. Nothing is obviously broken. Every design so far (iterations 0 to 10) ended off_track on every trial, with max_error at 0.060 to 0.068 and 1 to 2 line-loss events, so the known weakness (line loss at bends) is still unsolved, but no untested change has evidence strong enough to justify a revision with no race left to check it. Approving the best raced design is the lower-risk choice for the unseen-track race, which is scored from this design.
requested_changes: No change is requested for this final race. The candidate should race unchanged, because iteration 7 is the best raced design and each tested change from it (iterations 8, 9 and 10) scored lower.

For the record only: the next untested lever would be kp alone (3.0 to 3.5) with the 12 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.12 and base_speed 1.3 held, since iteration 8 confounded kp 3.5 with the 0.11 m track. This cannot be tested in this iteration, so it is noted for the team's records.
